messages.subject: stat_summary question
parts:
Hi there,

I need some help to create a profile plot with the follwoing command:

ggplot(testData, aes(x = variable, y = value, colour = treatment)) +
stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom = "line")

It works, if x is numeric but it doesn't display any line if x is of
class factor or character.
Did I do anything wrong?
If I use numeric, of course, the x-ticks do not contain the name of
the variable but a number instead.

Ciao

Hi,

you need to specify group in aes() like aes(x = variable, y = value,
colour = treatment, group = colour)

also see below:
http://kohske.wordpress.com/2010/12/27/faq-geom_line-doesnt-draw-lines/

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: stat_summary question
parts:
Hi:

To add to Kohske's comments, it also appears you want an average line; here's a toy example that shows how to do that as well, using group = 1 in conjunction with geom_smooth():

# Nine subjects in three treatment groups, each with responses on categories A-E
df <- data.frame(Treatment = factor(rep(1:3, each = 15)),
                 subj = rep(1:9, each = 5),
                 Category = rep(LETTERS[1:5], 9),
                 Response = rnorm(45))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Category, y = Response, groups = subj, colour = Treatment))
p + geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), colour = 'black', se = FALSE, size = 2)

If you'd like confidence bands around the average line, use se = TRUE (the default). This idea is borrowed from the example on pp. 50-51 of Hadley's book and adapted to categorical x variables. The variable names were chosen to minimize code writing in the ggplot() call.

What if one wants average lines per treatment plus an overall average line? It's more convenient to produce the treatment averages in a separate data frame first, and it's actually better to produce a separate plot for this purpose:

library(plyr)
# Average Response over Treatment x Category combinations
dfavg <- ddply(df, .(Treatment, Category), summarise, Average = mean(Response))
# Redo above plot on new data frame
q <- ggplot(dfavg, aes(x = Category, y = Average, color = Treatment, group = Treatment))
q + geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), color = 'black', size = 1.5)

# ...or you could try this instead:
p + geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), colour = 'black', se = FALSE, size = 1) +
    facet_grid(Treatment ~ .)

It helps to know that when the x-variable is categorical, geom_smooth() will produce group averages as the default 'smooth', so you can avoid the use of stat_summary() for this purpose. Of course, there are other contexts in which stat_summary() may be the better choice.

HTH,
Dennis
